# When --opt maps=true, Go-emitting platforms inject //line directives
# before each statement so the Go compiler attributes errors and stack
# traces back to the original SNGL source.
#
# The Go compiler resolves a relative //line path against the directory of
# the file carrying the directive, not the directory the build ran from, so
# the path is written relative to the output directory. Building from a
# subdirectory keeps the right answer ("../src/app.sngl") distinguishable
# from both the invocation path and a bare basename.

mkdir src
cp app.sngl src/app.sngl
rm app.sngl

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt=main=true --opt=maps=true --out=out src/app.sngl
exists out/model.go

# The directive names the source as reached from out/, where model.go lives.
grep '//line \.\./src/app\.sngl:' out/model.go

# And that is a path to something: the directive resolves to the real file.
exists out/../src/app.sngl

# An absolute path would resolve too, but only on the machine that built it.
! grep '//line /' out/model.go

# Sanity: without maps the directive is absent.
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt=main=true --out=out2 src/app.sngl
exists out2/model.go
! grep '//line ' out2/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main {
    var count = 0
    text(value=string(count))
    button(text="+", @click { count += 1 })
}
